en.heading: 5 December: South Korea's Trade Day changes name and date
en.origin: Trade Day developed from Export Day, designated by a government decision on 26 August 1964 to mark South Korea's achievement of 100 million US dollars in annual exports on 30 November. On 30 March 1973 the government consolidated several business-related observances into Export Day. The official name became Trade Day on 30 December 1988. A decree of 22 October 2012 moved the commemoration from 30 November to 5 December. Its current date therefore differs from the original export-achievement anniversary. For accurate interpretation, the historical starting point, early civic initiatives and the later government decision should remain distinguishable; a commemorative date is not automatically a general public holiday.
en.promoter: The South Korean government legally established or consolidated this national commemorative day after the predecessor events documented by its Ministry of the Interior.
en.purpose: Recognize exporters, trade workers and businesses and encourage understanding of international economic exchange.

Il 30 marzo 1973 il governo unì altre ricorrenze economiche alla giornata delle esportazioni. Il 30 dicembre 1988 la denominazione ufficiale cambiò in Trade Day. Un provvedimento del 22 ottobre 2012 spostò la giornata dal 30 novembre al 5 dicembre. La data moderna è quindi diversa dall'anniversario del primo traguardo. Per ricostruire correttamente l'origine occorre distinguere l'evento storico, le prime iniziative e la successiva decisione del governo; una ricorrenza non è automaticamente un giorno festivo nazionale.
it.promoter: Il governo sudcoreano ha istituito o accorpato questa ricorrenza pubblica dopo gli antecedenti documentati dal Ministero dell'Interno.
it.purpose: Riconoscere esportatori, lavoratori e imprese e diffondere la conoscenza degli scambi economici internazionali.

El 30 de marzo de 1973 el Gobierno integró otras jornadas empresariales en el Día de las Exportaciones. El 30 de diciembre de 1988 adoptó el nombre de Día del Comercio. Una reforma del 22 de octubre de 2012 trasladó la jornada del 30 de noviembre al 5 de diciembre; ya no coincide con el aniversario del primer objetivo. en.heading: 8 October: Korea's Veterans Association Day changed its anniversary
en.origin: Veterans Association Day recognizes former military personnel and the work of veterans' associations in South Korea. The national association was established in Busan on 1 February 1952. After organizational changes during the 1950s and membership in an international veterans federation in 1961, the government designated a Veterans Association Day on 8 June 1965, originally linked to 8 May. On 30 March 1973 it became a statutory commemoration, and on 19 June 2002 the government moved it from 8 May to 8 October. The association's founding and the modern date are distinct. It is important to distinguish the commemorated historical events and earlier public ceremonies from the later legal designation; the annual recurrence is governed by the national rules for this specific day.
en.promoter: The South Korean government and relevant public bodies institutionalized this day through the commemorative-day regulation, following its own distinct historical background.
en.purpose: Recognize veterans, their associations and the continuing social contributions of former service members.

Il 30 marzo 1973 entrò fra le commemorazioni legali e il 19 giugno 2002 la data cambiò dall'8 maggio all'8 ottobre. Nascita dell'associazione e data attuale non coincidono. È importante distinguere gli eventi storici ricordati e le prime iniziative pubbliche dal successivo riconoscimento legale; il calendario annuale segue le regole nazionali della ricorrenza.

en.heading: Fourth Friday in March: one day for the defenders of the West Sea
en.origin: West Sea Defense Day honours South Korean service members who died in several incidents at sea, including the 2002 Second Battle of Yeonpyeong, the 2010 sinking of the Cheonan and the 2010 shelling of Yeonpyeong. These are separate events and not one battle on the same date. The Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs reports that the government adopted the commemorative regulation on 22 March 2016. The first government ceremony was held on 25 March 2016; the annual recurrence is the fourth Friday of March. It must not be mistaken for the exact anniversary of each original incident. It is important to distinguish the commemorated historical events and earlier public ceremonies from the later legal designation; the annual recurrence is governed by the national rules for this specific day.

en.purpose: Remember those killed defending the West Sea, support their families and explain the different historical episodes.

en.heading: 5 October: World Koreans Day connects overseas communities
en.origin: World Koreans Day recognizes Korean communities living abroad and their ties with the Korean peninsula. Its place in the calendar was chosen in the week between National Foundation Day on 3 October and Hangeul Day on 9 October. The Ministry of the Interior explains that the government used the surrounding week to highlight the cultural identity of Korean communities overseas and exchanges with people in Korea. On 2 May 2007 the government formally established 5 October as a national statutory commemoration. The modern observance is not a United Nations world day, despite its international-sounding English title. It is important to distinguish the commemorated historical events and earlier public ceremonies from the later legal designation; the annual recurrence is governed by the national rules for this specific day.
en.promoter: The South Korean government and relevant public bodies institutionalized this day through the commemorative-day regulation, following its own distinct historical background.
en.purpose: Recognize overseas Korean communities, their cultural identity, their rights and their links with the country.
